title: Historical neural model architectures and parameter counts
population: Nine historical neural model families identified as M0–M8, with repeats r0 and r1.
metric: Recorded trainable parameter count per family.
units: Parameters; architecture widths are dimensionless node counts.
grouping: Model family; both repeats share the listed family topology and count.
uncertainty: Not applicable; architecture counts are deterministic records.
caption_tex: Historical neural architectures and complexity. (a) Computational graph of the largest family, M8, with each module labelled by the first family that contains it. M0--M2 use only the raw feedforward backbone; M3 adds a pointwise history encoder and M4 replaces it with a 32-unit GRU, both followed by mean and latest-value pooling; M5 adds a two-entry, eight-dimensional horizon embedding; M6 projects the first two of five schedule-basis values and M7 all five; M8 adds a bias-free 5-to-2 linear basis head. The concatenated width is 128 (M3, M4), 136 (M5) or 152 (M6--M8). (b) Component inclusion and recorded trainable parameter counts (1,346 to 10,796). Repeats r0 and r1 share each family's topology and count. Counts are from the public model-qualification summary. The figure describes structure, not predictive accuracy; fitted weights are not shown.
